source.version: Conference proceedings paper, 2026 International Conference on Creativity, Management, Education, Technology and Sciences (ICCMETS 2026), printed pages 179-190 (retrieved from iccmets.com/proceedings/2026/paper-18.pdf). The document prints no date and no DOI.
source.title_on_document: Generative AI and Student Creativity: Cognitive Scaffolding Tool or Constraint on Originality? An Empirical Investigation in Vietnamese Higher Education

supplement.holds: The document refers to no supplement or online appendix. All statistics are in the main text (Tables 1-3, pp. 184-185).

paper_design_summary: The paper reports a three-arm between-subjects experiment with 480 undergraduates at three Vietnamese universities: no AI (control), unconstrained use of an LLM (GPT-4o / Claude 3.5 Sonnet), and the same LLM under a structured protocol (own ideas first, then critique prompts, no copying). In one 90-minute session students proposed solutions to microplastic contamination and wrote a 600-word campaign brief. Trained raters coded fluency, flexibility, and elaboration, six experts rated originality, appropriateness, and overall creativity (CAT), and embedding cosine similarity measured homogenization within each condition.

studies.label: Three-arm experiment with Vietnamese undergraduates (problem-solving ideas and campaign brief)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Experimental condition: unaided control, unconstrained GenAI access, or structured scaffolding (Cognitive Anchor-Rebound Protocol) with the same LLM
assignment.quote: The quantitative phase deployed a randomized between-subjects experimental design with three conditions
assignment.locator: p. 182 (PDF p. 4), Section 3.1 Experimental Design; also Abstract p. 179: "three randomized experimental conditions"

arms.name: Unaided Control
arms.description: Creative problem-solving and ideation tasks with no digital devices, search engines, or AI interfaces.

arms.name: Unconstrained GenAI Access
arms.description: Unmonitored access to an LLM interface (GPT-4o / Claude 3.5 Sonnet), instructed: "You may use the AI tool in any manner you choose to complete this task."

arms.name: Structured Scaffolding
arms.description: Same LLM interface under the Cognitive Anchor-Rebound Protocol: Phase A at least three own ideas before opening the interface; Phase B critique and counter-factual prompts; Phase C synthesis without copying AI text.

participants.exclusions: None reported. Section 3.1 gives n = 160 per condition and Table 1 reports n = 160 per condition (N = 480) with F(2, 477), so the counts at assignment and at analysis are the same. The paper does not describe attrition or exclusions, nor the randomization procedure.
participants.who: Undergraduates in three disciplinary clusters (Humanities & Social Sciences, Business & Management, Design, Media & Technology; n = 160 each); 58.3% female; mean age 20.4 (SD 1.35). Recruited by stratified random sampling at Vietnam National University (Hanoi), The University of Danang, and HUTECH (Ho Chi Minh City).
participants.quote: A total of 480 undergraduate students participated across three broad disciplinary clusters.
participants.locator: p. 182 (PDF p. 4), Section 3.2; participant matrix p. 183 (PDF p. 5); Table 1 header p. 184 (PDF p. 6)

ai_tool.how_used: Unconstrained arm: free use of the chatbot in any manner. Scaffolded arm: same chatbot, but students first wrote at least three own ideas, then used critique and counter-factual prompts, then synthesized without copying AI text blocks.

task.description: Task 1: Alternative Solutions Task, proposing innovative sustainable solutions to urban microplastic contamination in the Mekong Delta agricultural belt. Task 2: a 600-word conceptual campaign brief for a socio-technological enterprise on rural education equity in Vietnam.
task.duration: Both tasks within one 90-minute timed session (p. 183, Section 3.3)

outcomes.name: Originality (CAT, expert-rated, 1-7)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Six independent domain experts (two professors in environmental social science, two creative design directors, two innovation hub leads) rated the project briefs on 7-point scales; Cronbach's alpha = .91 (p. 183, Section 3.4 item 2). Listed among the MANOVA's "primary dependent variables" (p. 184).

contrasts.reported: Unconstrained 3.41 (0.94), n = 160 vs Control 4.82 (1.15), n = 160; omnibus F(2, 477) = 165.23, p < .001, eta^2 = .409 (Table 1); Tukey post hoc p < .001, d = -1.34 (p. 184). The abstract reports d = -0.58, p < .001 for the same contrast (p. 179).
contrasts.locator: p. 184, Table 1 and Section 4.1 first bullet; p. 179, Abstract; p. 187, Discussion box (d = -1.34)

contrasts.reported: Scaffolded 5.44 (0.88), n = 160 vs Control 4.82 (1.15), n = 160; Tukey p < .001, d = 0.61
contrasts.locator: p. 184, Table 1 and Section 4.1 second bullet

outcomes.name: Semantic diversity across students (reported as mean pairwise cosine similarity; sign reversed)
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Submissions embedded with OpenAI text-embedding-3-large, described as a 1536-dimensional space; mean pairwise cosine similarity within each condition and task, plus a Semantic Dispersion Index = 1 - CosSim (Table 2). The paper reports similarity, so higher values mean less diversity; direction below is stated for diversity. Named among the MANOVA primary DVs as "Semantic Distance" (p. 184).

contrasts.reported: Mean pairwise cosine similarity (SD): Unconstrained 0.689 (0.061), dispersion 0.311 vs Control 0.412 (0.084), dispersion 0.588; t(318) = 34.21, p < .001, d = 3.79 (higher similarity = less diversity)
Scaffolded 0.465 (0.072), dispersion 0.535 vs Control 0.412 (0.084), dispersion 0.588. No test reported (Table 2 gives means and SDs only).
Scaffolded 0.465 (0.072) vs Unconstrained 0.689 (0.061) mean pairwise cosine similarity. No test reported.

diversity_detail.metric: Mean pairwise cosine similarity between submissions; Semantic Dispersion Index = 1 - mean cosine similarity
diversity_detail.embedding_model: OpenAI text-embedding-3-large (paper states a 1536-dimensional vector space)
diversity_detail.computed_over: All pairs of student submissions within the same condition and the same task (p. 183, Section 3.4 item 3). Table 2 gives one value per condition and does not say whether it pools the two tasks.
diversity_detail.uncertainty: A t-test with t(318) is reported for Unconstrained vs Control. The 318 degrees of freedom match 160 + 160 participants rather than the number of pairs; the paper does not explain what unit the test uses or what the SD in Table 2 is taken over.
diversity_detail.notes: statistics_available uses figure_only for the scaffolded contrasts as the closest code: Table 2 prints arm means and SDs, but no test and no count of pairs.

company_involvement.description: No company involvement or funding is stated.

eligibility.reason: As written, the paper reports random assignment of 480 undergraduates (160 per arm) to no AI, unconstrained LLM use, or structured LLM use (p. 182), with expert CAT ratings, rater-coded TTCT scores, and embedding similarity of the outputs (pp. 183-185). All three criteria are met on the text. The paper has serious internal inconsistencies (see open_questions) and does not describe the randomization procedure, so the record needs a data-integrity check before any estimate is pooled.

one_line_finding: Compared with no AI, unconstrained LLM use raised fluency (11.45 vs 5.12) but lowered expert-rated originality (3.41 vs 4.82, d = -1.34) and raised mean pairwise cosine similarity (0.689 vs 0.412), while structured scaffolding raised originality (5.44, d = 0.61) and overall creativity (5.51 vs 4.48) (pp. 184-185, Tables 1-2).
open_questions: Abstract and results disagree on fluency: abstract F(2,477) = 48.21, eta^2 = .168 (p. 179) vs Table 1 F = 284.15, eta^2 = .543 (p. 184).
Abstract and results disagree on the originality effect of unconstrained AI vs control: abstract d = -0.58 (p. 179) vs text d = -1.34 (p. 184, repeated p. 187).
The ASCII figure on p. 185 places Control originality near 5-6 and Scaffolded near 6-7 on the CAT scale, while Table 1 gives means of 4.82 and 5.44.

Table 3 (p. 185) and its text (p. 186) disagree on significance: Unconstrained Prompt Count -.241 carries no star in Model 3 but the text says p < .01; Iterative Counter-Prompts .389* in the table vs p < .001 in the text. The star legend prints '* p < .05, p < .01, * p < .001'.
The MANOVA is said to use four primary DVs (Fluency, Flexibility, Originality, Semantic Distance), but the reported Pillai's trace test is F(12, 946) (p. 184).
The diversity t-test has t(318) degrees of freedom, which matches two arms of 160 people, although the measure is described as pairwise similarity (pp. 183, 185). The unit of the test is unclear.
The paper does not say which task (Task 1 solutions or Task 2 brief) each TTCT score and the embedding similarity come from; CAT ratings are of the project briefs (p. 183).

The reference list is truncated mid-entry (Dwivedi et al., ending 'Bose#', p. 190) and many in-text citations (e.g., Kasneci et al., 2023; Hutchins, 1995; Mollick & Mollick, 2023; Jansson & Smith, 1991; Torrance, 1966) have no reference entry.
No randomization procedure, attrition, ethics approval, preregistration, or data availability is reported. 'Stratified random sampling' (p. 182) describes recruitment, not assignment.
Should a paper with these inconsistencies enter pooled estimates at all, or be held as core-eligible pending verification?
notes: Single-session lab experiment ('laboratory conditions', p. 189, Limitations item 1; 90-minute timed session, p. 183). Table 3 (p. 185) is a hierarchical regression of originality on prompting behaviors among the 320 AI users (Conditions 2 and 3 pooled); it is not a randomized contrast and is not coded as an outcome. Qualitative results (36 interviews, p. 183; 88.4% of unconstrained students built on one of the AI's listed options and recurring themes appeared across 71% of unconstrained essays, p. 186) are descriptive and not coded. No outcome was measured after AI was removed, so there is no after_ai evidence despite the search lane guess. The search record's 'd = -0.58' comes from the abstract and conflicts with the body text.
